Speed release on top of [v2.22](../../releases/tag/v2.22). Changes how the two
tubes share a charge. **Re-run Learn Powder after installing** - none of this
reaches an existing profile until it is re-fitted.

Personal fork, developed and tested on one machine with one powder. It dispenses
gunpowder charges for ammunition reloading - verify weights independently.

| File | Board | |
|---|---|---|
| `opentrickler-v2.3-pico2_w.uf2` | Raspberry Pi Pico **2** W (RP2350) | developed and tested on this |
| `opentrickler-v2.3-pico_w.uf2` | Raspberry Pi Pico W (RP2040) | builds, PIO fix from v2.22, still unconfirmed |

Install over USB BOOTSEL. v2.22 and earlier have OTA defects that only a
BOOTSEL install clears. Includes everything in v2.22.

**Hardware status:** the landing trim and handoff cap below are measured on
hardware (16/16 passes, mean error -0.0007 gr). The coarse taper is modelled
and built, not yet measured - it needs a fresh Learn fit to exist at all. If
your first session after Learn throws over, say so with the session CSV.

## What was slow

A session at 26.5 gr ran 11.5 s a throw: the coarse tube for under 2 s, the
fine tube for over 9. The fit was sizing the handoff on the coarse tube's stop
scatter *at full bulk speed*, so a fast bulk demanded a huge handoff - half the
charge, 13 grains, went through the fine tube at 1.4 gr/s. Live tuning narrows
the handoff 5% per five clean throws and could never dig out of that.

Before that, a global handoff fitted at one charge weight could exceed a lighter
target entirely; the coarse stop then fired on the first reading and the fine
tube delivered the whole charge alone (`coarse_s = 0.00` in the session CSV).

## Coarse taper

The coarse runs flat out to a taper window before its stop point, then ramps
down to a **landing speed** so it is crawling when the stop fires. The fit
sweeps that landing speed from the ladder's slowest rung upward and sizes the
handoff on the stop scatter at the landing speed, not at full speed. Crawling
the last grain or two costs about a second and shrinks the handoff by the ratio
of the two speeds.

On a model with numbers matching the tested hardware: old fit 10.3 s, new fit
8.2 s (bulk 5 rps, landing 0.8 rps, handoff 2.3 gr). The fine tube's
exponential approach is now the largest term.

Back-off after a failed confirm slows the landing 0.7x as well as widening the
handoff. A live over where the bulk ran long drops the landing 0.85x. A live
coarse speed-up keeps the taper window the same width.

## Handoff

- Capped at half the target wherever it is used and after every live-tuning
  write. The coarse tube always carries at least half the charge.
- The fit no longer floors the handoff at the fine taper width. Below the taper
  the fine simply picks up part way down its ramp; prediction already covers
  what is in the air.
- Live "tighten" only ever narrows. It used to be able to raise the handoff
  through a floor tied to the taper, which only grows.

## Learned landing trim

The charge loop ends a throw as soon as the reading is inside the bracket below
target, so results sat low (mean -0.030 gr against a 0.06 bracket). A per-profile
trim now steers the 12-throw mean to zero (gain 0.15, clamped to half a
bracket). Measured: mean -0.0007 gr over 16 throws.

The landing-speed margin is measured to the nearer bracket edge rather than to
the target, and the adjustment runs every four passes instead of after a
five-clean streak.

## Portal

- Live status poll has a 3 s timeout, so one dropped request no longer freezes
  the display.
- Learn results show the coarse taper window beside Coarse Kp and the coarse
  landing speed as the coarse minimum.

**No EEPROM layout change.** Settings and profiles carry over, but re-run Learn
Powder to get the taper.
